title: Elimination Game
summary: Given a list arr containing all integers from 1 to n in strictly increasing order, repeatedly apply the following steps: start from the left and remove the first element and every other element to the right; then start from the right and remove the last element and every other element to the left.
statement: Given a list arr containing all integers from 1 to n in strictly increasing order, repeatedly apply the following steps: start from the left and remove the first element and every other element to the right; then start from the right and remove the last element and every other element to the left. Continue alternating between left-to-right and right-to-left removals until only one element remains. Return the last remaining element.
constraints: Each round deletes the first encountered element, then every other element; direction alternates.
When only one element remains, stop without performing another round.
hints: Survivors always form an arithmetic progression; you do not need to store them.
Track the first survivor, gap, remaining count, and direction.
Advance the first survivor when deleting from the left or when the remaining count is odd. Then halve count, double gap, and reverse direction.
There are O(log n) rounds. An equivalent recursive reflection formula is f(n)=2*(floor(n/2)+1−f(floor(n/2))), with f(1)=1.
editorial: Deleting alternate elements doubles the gap. From the left, the first element is always removed; from the right, it is removed exactly when the count is odd. Update the head before halving the count. The recursive formula reflects the next round’s survivor index within the even numbers, providing another way to understand alternating direction.

tests.explanation: The surviving lists are [2,4,6,8], then [2,6] when deleting from the right, then [6].
First [2,4,6] survives. The right-to-left round removes 6 and 2, leaving 4.
